text: DBIM SCHEME PAGES PUT EACH PART WHERE A READER LOOKS FOR IT, IN DBIM'S DETAIL LAYOUT. The live pages file content under whatever heading was to hand — PM-DAKSH's About is its application steps and required documents, NOS's Benefits ends with its documents and dates, Pre-Matric's About holds its conditions of eligibility. sortTopics (lib/website-dbim/prose.ts, with tests) moves each labelled part — eligibility, benefits, required documents, timelines, how to apply, and a numbered list that opens with Register/Apply/Visit — to its own section, its words and label kept. Application Process reads Where to Apply → Steps to Apply → Required Documents → Important Timelines. The page takes DBIM 3.0 Figure 71's layout as the Organisation page draws it: the grey side box carries the scheme's name, its standing and one Apply Now (the handoff's Filled Button, labelled just that), with On This Page beneath it; the reference's VISIT bar and Scheme Versions box are gone. The master's editorial note is no longer shown.
